This contradicts the requirement to make the 'strongest case' for defensibility; a truly strong defense would argue that critical rationality *provides* a non-inductive form of epistemic justification (e.g., via verisimilitude or the logic of situational analysis) that makes the preference rational, rather than dismissing it as an unjustified gamble.
